testimonials.text: The most interesting aspects were the surgical decision-making, especially choosing between ORIF, percutaneous fixation, and primary hip replacement, as well as the importance of fracture patterns and patient context. I also found the management of complex cases and the concept of doing less is more particularly valuable.
The most interesting thing I found was the practical approach to managing complex fractures, especially how surgeons adapted techniques in resource-limited environments.
I found the interactive case studies and guest speaker sessions most interesting, they brought real-world context to the material and made complex ideas easier to understand.
The real-life case discussions and step-by-step surgical techniques were the most interesting aspects, as they clearly demonstrated practical applications of the concepts.
The case discussions helped me ponder over our cases in a more holistic approach.
Learning from case scenario world wide makes it easier to know what best in acetabulum fracture management.
